% Abstract — Depth Profiling of Recursive LLM Generation Chains
\begin{abstract}
As LLM outputs re-enter training corpora and seed further generation, understanding how recursive generation reshapes text distributions is critical for data provenance and corpus curation---yet existing detectors answer only the binary human-or-machine question, ignoring \emph{generation depth}: we introduce \emph{depth profiling} to address this gap.
We decompose distributional drift under recursive generation into location and shape components, revealing an asymmetry we term \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators from five families, NLL location features drift monotonically with depth (effect size $d{=}0.74$--$1.05$) while three shape features remain near-stationary ($d < 0.10$), with entropy std intermediate ($d{=}0.46$).
Prior work documents \emph{what converges}; the central finding here is \emph{what is approximately preserved}: shape stability complements location drift for ordinal depth grading without per-generator calibration, achieving leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) and 3-class F1\,=\,0.762 (gen-0 seeds shared across generators; \S\ref{sec:generation}) under leave-one-generator-out evaluation; an end-to-end classifier reaches 3-class F1\,=\,0.905 (6-gen LOGO; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction tuning compresses DDR, bounding current applicability to base models.
\end{abstract}

input.old_string: \looseness=-1 We hypothesize that DDR reflects an empirical regularity of base-model autoregressive generation: recursive inputs compress the token-level NLL distribution monotonically (Appendix~\ref{app:nll-distribution}), producing location drift independent of the token-selection mechanism. Shape features (extreme ranges, tail decay) are bounded by architectural constraints (vocabulary size, softmax temperature) rather than input statistics, explaining their stability under recursive compression. Controlled ablations---greedy decoding, temperature modulation, and semantic-constraint attenuation---support this (Appendices~\ref{app:decoding-strategy}--\ref{app:prompt-type}); ANOVA quantifies the asymmetry: $\eta^2_{\text{depth}}{=}0.34$--$0.37$ for location vs.\ ${<}0.01$ for shape (${>}48{\times}$; Appendix~\ref{app:variance-decomposition}; Granger causality tests support the predictive direction, Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}). DDR is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}---retraining erodes tail via weight updates, whereas inference-chain drift shifts only location---and complements concurrent iterative-generation studies (Appendix~\ref{app:iterative-comparison}). Preliminary batch-level estimates suggest depth constitutes a new analytical dimension for corpus auditing, with contamination estimation reaching ${\pm}3$--$4$\% at $n{=}1{,}000$ (Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}); instruction tuning compresses DDR (QLoRA: F1\,=\,0.89--0.91; Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), while cross-domain signal persists (F1\,=\,0.74--0.75; Appendix~\ref{app:domain}).

\paragraph{Mechanistic interpretation.}
\looseness=-1 DDR reflects an empirical regularity of base-model autoregressive generation: recursive inputs compress the token-level NLL distribution monotonically (Appendix~\ref{app:nll-distribution}), shifting location features independently of the token-selection mechanism.
Shape features resist this compression because they are architecturally bounded---entropy max is capped by $\log|V|$, and tail decay reflects softmax long-tail geometry rather than input statistics---explaining their near-stationarity across generators and depths.
Controlled ablations (greedy decoding, temperature modulation, semantic-constraint attenuation; Appendices~\ref{app:decoding-strategy}--\ref{app:prompt-type}) corroborate this account.
ANOVA quantifies the asymmetry: $\eta^2_{\text{depth}}{=}0.34$--$0.37$ for location vs.\ $\eta^2_{\text{gen}}{<}0.009$ (${>}48{\times}$; Appendix~\ref{app:variance-decomposition}; Granger causality supports the predictive direction, Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}), indicating that generation depth is a more fundamental analytical dimension than generator architecture---recursive generation imposes a universal compression trajectory that transcends model family.
DDR is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}: retraining erodes tail coverage via weight updates, whereas inference-chain drift shifts only location; DDR complements concurrent iterative-generation studies (Appendix~\ref{app:iterative-comparison}).

\paragraph{Failure modes and practical scope.}
\looseness=-1 The gen-1$\to$gen-2 boundary is the primary classification failure point (depth-2 error rate\,=\,48.4\%; Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}): the gen-0$\to$gen-1 transition produces the largest distributional shift, so depth-2 texts carry insufficient accumulated drift beyond gen-1 for reliable separation.
Deeper generations ($\geq$gen-3) show monotonically decreasing error rates ($\leq$29.2\%), confirming that DDR signal strengthens with chain length.
Batch-level contamination estimation reaches ${\pm}3$--$4$\% at $n{=}1{,}000$ (Appendix~\ref{app:error-analysis}); instruction tuning compresses DDR (QLoRA: F1\,=\,0.89--0.91; Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), while cross-domain signal persists (F1\,=\,0.74--0.75; Appendix~\ref{app:domain}).

lines: \paragraph{Mechanistic interpretation.}

\looseness=-1 DDR reflects an empirical regularity of base-model autoregressive generation: recursive inputs compress the token-level NLL distribution monotonically (Appendix~\ref{app:nll-distribution}), shifting location features independently of the token-selection mechanism.

Shape features resist this compression because they are architecturally bounded---entropy max is capped by $\log|V|$, and tail decay reflects softmax long-tail geometry rather than input statistics---explaining their near-stationarity across generators and depths.

\subsection{Comparison with Detection Baselines}
\label{sec:results-baselines}

We next ask whether existing detection methods---designed for binary real-vs-synthetic classification---incidentally capture depth structure, repurposing four detection scores as ordinal depth predictors under identical XGBoost and LOGO conditions (Table~\ref{tab:baselines}).
The strongest baseline is a 4-detector + surface feature ensemble (binary F1\,=\,0.708), which pools four detection scores with TTR and hapax ratio; among individual detectors, Avg-LogProb provides the most meaningful single-feature comparison.

Individual detection scores (N/A) share the reference-model forward pass; per-method timing is not separately profiled. XGBoost uses 7 handcrafted scalar features (one 410M reference); QLoRA (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}) uses the full token sequence---an information-asymmetric ceiling, not a fair comparison.}

\midrule

\end{table}

The 7-feature ensemble matches the 4-detector+surface ensemble on binary F1 (0.705 vs.\ 0.708; Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-ci}) at ${\sim}2.4\times$ lower cost, though the latter leads by 2.1\,pp on 3-class F1 (0.795 vs.\ 0.774); both surpass individual detectors by 3.0--16.6\,pp.
DDR's contribution is the decomposition into location-sensitive and shape-stable components (\S\ref{sec:discussion}), achieving comparable depth discrimination with a single 410M reference model; ordinal-specific methods (CORAL, Frank-Hall) yield comparable F1 (Appendix~\ref{app:classifier}).
Concurrent iterative-generation studies use different chain operators (back-translation, rephrasing) and target different phenomena (factuality, convergence dynamics), precluding direct inclusion as depth classification baselines (Appendix~\ref{app:iterative-comparison}).

lines: \looseness=-1 DDR reflects an empirical regularity of base-model autoregressive generation: recursive inputs compress the token-level NLL distribution monotonically (Appendix~\ref{app:nll-distribution}), shifting location features independently of the token-selection mechanism.

Shape features resist this compression because they are architecturally bounded---entropy max is capped by $\log|V|$, and tail decay reflects softmax long-tail geometry rather than input statistics---explaining their near-stationarity across generators and depths.

Controlled ablations (Appendices~\ref{app:decoding-strategy}--\ref{app:prompt-type}) and ANOVA corroborate this: $\eta^2_{\text{depth}}{=}0.34$--$0.37$ for location vs.\ $\eta^2_{\text{gen}}{<}0.009$ (${>}48{\times}$; Appendix~\ref{app:variance-decomposition}; Granger causality: Appendix~\ref{app:ddr-causality}), indicating that generation depth is a more fundamental analytical dimension than generator architecture---recursive generation imposes a universal compression trajectory that transcends model family.

+DDR is distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}---retraining erodes tail via weight updates, while DDR shifts only location---and complements concurrent iterative-generation studies (Appendix~\ref{app:iterative-comparison}).
\paragraph{Failure modes and practical scope.}
